label: conj:im-q-physical-role
title: Physical role of $\mathrm{Im}(q)$: a substrate moduli parameter not constrained by current QOU observables, with three candidate roles (chirality / phase coordinate / non-Hermitian deformation).
html:
Conjecture (physical role of Im(q)). The substrate parameter q admits a complex extension (prop:q-zero-complex-extension). The current QOU framework's observables (categorical masses \mathfrak{m}_{q,\mathcal{K}} = |\mathrm{tr}_M| and per-braid mass tower) are real-valued and insensitive to \mathrm{Im}(q) at leading order under modulus projection (\mathrm{Im}(q) shifts both numerator and denominator of mass ratios in tandem via the modulus operation). The physical role of \mathrm{Im}(q) — if any — must therefore be sought in observables not currently in the framework.

This conjecture catalogues three candidate roles, each testable against a specific observable class. All three are now settled on the archimedean side of the substrate wall — the evaluation at q_0 — and all three remain open on the fibre, where q is a formal variable and \mathrm{Im}(q) is unconstrained. The conjecture is therefore restated as a fibre-level question; the archimedean findings are recorded in the section Reality of \mathfrak{Q}_\beta at the substrate below.

Exclusions for Im(q)

Per rem:im-q-vs-p-skew, Im(q) is NOT:

  • The EM / P_{\mathrm{skew}} channel (this is a real-q mechanism)
  • A fourth calibration input (the 3-CAL count is cohomologically forced)
  • An observable in the current framework (mass formula uses |\cdot|)
  • Equal to \mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta))) — Im(q) is a parameter; Im(tr_M) is the value induced

Reality of \mathfrak{Q}_\beta at the substrate

The framework does possess an \mathrm{Im}(q)-sensitive observable, which the opening paragraph's "not currently in the framework" did not anticipate: the decay Q-value \mathfrak{Q}_\beta. Its closed form carries the modulus on a single factor, so unlike the mass formula it does not project \mathrm{Im}(q) away. Since \mathfrak{Q}_\beta is a measured Q-value it is real, and \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{Q}_\beta = 0 is one real equation on (\mathrm{Re}\,q, \mathrm{Im}\,q).

candidate conclusion at q_0 scope carrier
(i) chirality the identification \text{chirality} = (q \mapsto \bar q) holds exactly on \lvert q\rvert = 1; the substrate sits 18.83\,\% of q_0 away from it (b) qou:QOU.QBeta.conj_eq_inv_iff_modulus_one
(ii) phase dual to CAL-2 \mathrm{Im}\,q = 0 on the whole admissible set (b) qou:QOU.QBeta.im_qbeta_zero_iff_e2
(iii) non-Hermitian premise correct; open, but re-scoped — the framework does carry a categorical decay rate, and that rate is built entirely at real q (a) qou:QOU.QBeta.two_width_mechanisms_are_independent

For (i), the corpus's own chirality operation is the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} — the mirror knot, J_{\bar K}(q) = J_K(q^{-1}) — and \bar q = q^{-1} exactly when \lvert q\rvert = 1. At q_0 the mirror is q_0^{-1} \approx 0.9009182840, a real number carrying no \mathrm{Im}(q), so the chirality content sought here is already present at real q as the P_{\mathrm{skew}} part of the bar decomposition.

For (iii), a width obtained as \mathfrak{D} = \hbar / \mathfrak{Q} with \mathfrak{Q} real is a different mechanism from a width obtained as -2\,\mathrm{Im}\,E: on a real spectrum the second vanishes identically while the first does not. That much is arithmetic and is scope (a), not (b).

What it does not establish is that the framework realises the first mechanism. CAL-2 is named the neutron \beta-sector bar-skew channel P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}, and the corpus relates it to the CAL-2 proxy by \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}; but a width and a lifetime are reciprocal by definition, so if P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} is the width then P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} is the neutron lifetime, 878.4\;\mathrm{s}, and not an energy. Defining P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} := \hbar/\mathfrak{Q}_\beta instead is dimensionally consistent but gives 8.40 \times 10^{-22}\;\mathrm{s}, which is 24.02 orders of magnitude from that lifetime. Equivalently the neutron's actual width \Gamma_n = \hbar/\tau_n = 7.49 \times 10^{-19}\;\mathrm{eV} sits 24.02 orders below \mathfrak{Q}_\beta.

So \mathfrak{Q}_\beta and \Gamma_n are independent properties of one decay rather than reciprocals: a Q-value is fixed by mass differences alone, while a width additionally requires the coupling and the phase-space integral. The framework reproduces the Q-value to 0.17\,\% — that result is untouched — and \Gamma_n is a width the reciprocal mechanism demonstrably fails to produce.

The coupling and the phase-space integral are, however, supplied elsewhere in the corpus, which an earlier version of this section denied. The rate formula of hadron half-life is

  \Gamma_\beta
  =
  \frac{\lvert\mathcal{W}(q)\rvert^2\,\mu_0}{2\pi^3}
   \cdot
  [2]_q
   \cdot
  \lvert\mathcal{M}_q\rvert^2
   \cdot
  f(Q),
  \qquad f(Q) \propto Q^5 ,

whose coupling has a closed form — the canonical Markov trace of the T_{3,5} braid word in H_3(q), \mathcal{W}(q) = q^2(q^{12}+q^8-1)/(q^2+1)^2, with \mathcal{W}(1) = 1/4. So the missing object is not the rate.

This re-scopes candidate (iii) rather than discharging it, and it re-scopes it against the candidate. Every factor above is real for real q: a modulus squared, [2]_q = q + q^{-1}, a trace ratio, and Q^5. The framework therefore produces a decay width with no \mathrm{Im}\,q anywhere — the same posture the mass formula takes. What (iii) needs is not a width the framework lacks but a reason a width should require \mathrm{Im}\,q when the framework's own does not. Scope (a): this says the corpus's construction needs no \mathrm{Im}\,q, not that no construction does.

What the rate formula genuinely lacks is its scale, not its shape. The weak-scale crossing count N_v in v = N_v\,\mathfrak{E}_\times\,\mu_0 is undetermined, so G_F enters numerically from experiment; the Lean carrier all_six_agree says so in its own docstring, and the Fermi-relation block lists it as open computation 1. Since m_e = 3\mathfrak{E}_\times\mu_0, both \mathfrak{E}_\times and \mu_0 cancel and N_v = 3v/m_e = 1445519.51 \pm 0.37 is q-independent — carrying no anchor and no Markov-parameter convention.

Three candidate physical roles

Candidate (i) — chirality / orientation parameter

In the Kashaev regime (q a root of unity, q = e^{2\pi i/N}), the q-deformed Hecke algebra produces N-fold quantum symmetries whose Markov traces give hyperbolic volumes (Kashaev volume conjecture). For complex q = |q| e^{i \arg q} near the unit circle, \arg q is naturally a chirality coordinate — positive arg gives clockwise braid orientation; negative arg gives counterclockwise. The categorical mass formula is invariant under q \mapsto \bar q (complex conjugation under modulus projection), consistent with mass being chirality-invariant.

Testable (fibre). Scope (b) at q_0, by the section above. The surviving question is whether \arg q is a chirality coordinate on the fibre, in the Kashaev regime \lvert q\rvert = 1 where \bar q = q^{-1} and the two candidate operations coincide. There the identification is correct, and the open part is whether a fibre-level chirality-sensitive element has an archimedean image at all. Superseded archimedean form: does the framework's prediction for an explicitly chirality-sensitive observable (e.g., parity-violating decay asymmetry; CP violation in K^0-\bar K^0 mixing) require \arg q \neq 0?

Candidate (ii) — phase coordinate dual to CAL-2

CAL-2 (m_\mu/m_e = 206.7682830) gives one real equation on two real unknowns (\mathrm{Re}(q), \mathrm{Im}(q)). The solution set is an Apollonius circle in the complex q-plane (center \approx 1.010, radius \approx 0.100 per the formal derivation). The framework's real-axis solution q_0 \approx 1.10998 is one point on this circle; Im(q) is the arc coordinate parametrizing the other admissible q values.

Testable (fibre). Scope (b) at q_0. This candidate states its own closure condition — "if only real solutions exist, candidate (ii) is closed" — and the second constraint it asks for is \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{Q}_\beta = 0, from the CAL-2 proxy itself. Under both complex extensions the corpus supports, the zero set factors as y \cdot (\text{branch}) with every branch empty on \mathrm{Re}\,q > 1/2, and the Apollonius circle above lies entirely in that half-plane: its centre is 1.0099145 and its radius 0.1000641, so its leftmost point is 0.9098504 — closed forms 1/(1-k^2), k/(1-k^2) and 1/(1+k) with k^2 = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/(m_\mu/m_e), reproduced by the_apollonius_circle_from_cal2_reproduces_exactly_probe.py (4/4), which also records that no q_0 enters: CAL-2 is the equation that defines q_0, so neither the anchor question nor the CODATA vintage reaches these three numbers. Only the two real intersections survive, and the circle's arc coordinate is not a live degree of freedom. The surviving question is the fibre one: whether \mathrm{Im}(q) parametrises anything at the level of the formal variable, where no reality condition is imposed.

Candidate (iii) — non-Hermitian deformation / open-system parameter

The Hoefsmit seminormal Hecke representation has real-coefficient matrices for q > 0 real, giving unitary H_n(q) representations. For complex q with |q| \neq 1, unitarity breaks: representations become non-unitary; eigenvalues become complex. In quantum mechanics, non-Hermitian operators arise in open systems (decay, dissipation, resonance widths).

Testable. Open. The exhibit asked for — a \Gamma the reciprocal mechanism fails to produce — is the neutron's own, by 24.02 orders of magnitude (see the section above), so this candidate's obstacle is not retired. Original form: do decay widths (Γ for unstable particles — W, Z, top, resonances) correlate with the Im(q) needed to make Hecke representations describe their non-Hermitian dynamics? Most decay widths in the Standard Model have categorical interpretations open in the QOU framework.

Obstacles to a current proof

Each candidate was stated as requiring an observable the framework does not yet provide. Two of those three requirements are met by observables already present; the third is not.

  • (i) asked for a chirality-sensitive observable. The corpus already carries a chirality operation — the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1}, the mirror knot — and it acts at real q.
  • (ii) asked for a second CAL-2-like constraint. \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{Q}_\beta = 0 is one, supplied by the CAL-2 proxy itself.
  • (iii) asked for a categorical formula for decay widths \Gamma. That requirement is met: hadron half-life states one, with a closed-form coupling. What stands in (iii)'s way is the opposite of an absence — the corpus's rate is manifestly real at real q, so it exhibits a width needing no \mathrm{Im}\,q. Separately, the reciprocal mechanism \Gamma = \hbar/\mathfrak{Q}_\beta misses \Gamma_n by 24.02 orders of magnitude, and the rate's overall scale is imported pending the weak-scale crossing count N_v.

The framework's mass formula explicitly projects away Im(q) content via |\cdot|, so no mass observable can detect Im(q) directly. The candidate roles are all in non-mass observables.

Connection to other conjectures

  • conj:lepton-mass-tower-canonical F_ℓ — the canonical lepton-mass formula is Im(q)-robust (modulus projection invariance); F_ℓ does NOT distinguish the three candidate Im(q) roles. Hence the F_ℓ conjecture is consistent with ALL three candidates.
  • prop:rho-k-pair-gen-canonical-form — similarly Im(q)-robust at LO.
  • The complex-q machinery is decoupled from the mass-formula closure; closing the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta residual or deriving F_ℓ does not require resolving Im(q)'s role.

Default value: Im(q) = 0

In the absence of an Im(q)-sensitive observable, the framework's canonical choice is \mathrm{Im}(q_0) = 0 (real q). This is:

  • Computationally simple: real Hecke arithmetic, real \mathrm{tr}_M, real masses.
  • Empirically sufficient: all known mass observables fit with real q_0 to the precision documented in per-observable-100x-status.witness.json.
  • Structurally forced at the archimedean layer, and no longer a convention. qou:QOU.QBeta.im_qbeta_zero_iff_e2 derives \mathrm{Im}(q_0) = 0 from the reality of \mathfrak{Q}_\beta on \mathrm{Re}\,q > 1/2, which contains the whole CAL-2 admissible set. The Im-sensitive measurement this clause was waiting for is \mathfrak{Q}_\beta itself.
  • NOT forced on the fibre: nothing in the framework's cohomological discipline requires \mathrm{Im}(q) = 0 for the formal variable, and the fibre-vs-observable separation makes that the layer where the three candidates remain live.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs — real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
